arguments.claim: Epstein's NPA with USAO-SDFL did not bar Maxwell's prosecution by USAO-SDNY
arguments.evidence: The NPA does not bind USAO-SDNY; it was an agreement with a different prosecutorial office

arguments.claim: Maxwell's indictment complied with the statute of limitations
arguments.evidence: 18 U.S.C. § 3283 extended the time to bring charges of sexual abuse for offenses committed before the statute's enactment

arguments.claim: District Court did not abuse its discretion in denying Maxwell's Rule 33 motion for new trial
arguments.evidence: The motion was based on one juror's erroneous answers during voir dire, which the court found insufficient to warrant a new trial

arguments.claim: District Court's response to jury note did not result in constructive amendment or prejudicial variance
arguments.evidence: The court's response remained within the allegations of the indictment
The Second Circuit identified no procedural errors in the District Court's sentencing

arguments.claim: Facts should be viewed in the light most favorable to the Government on appeal from conviction
arguments.evidence: Citing United States v. Litwok, 678 F.3d 208, 210-11 (2d Cir. 2012)
